effects.note: Only to identify spells on the spirit magic lists of your primary and wandering spirits, and only when they are cast within the area.

effects.target: saving throws to resist spells on your primary and wandering spirits' spirit magic lists, and spell-like abilities duplicating them
you are never considered flat-footed against attack rolls made by those spells
effects.note: Scoped to the same list of spells as the bonuses above.

sense-spirit-magic.notes: Both bonus types are stated as circumstance, so they are emitted rather than guessed.

effects.target: your eyes shine blood red and you see the vital areas of creatures within 30 feet as a warm glow, letting you make sneak attacks with any manufactured weapon exactly as the rogue ability does
effects.note: Recorded as a granted ability rather than a damage spec - the extra dice only exist on an attack that qualifies as a sneak attack.

effects.target: The sneak attack deals an extra 1d6 points of damage, rising by 1d6 for every 3 caster levels past 3rd to a maximum of +5d6 at 15th level, and it stacks with other sources of precision damage.
effects.note: This damage belongs to your weapon attacks, not to the spell, and only lands when the sneak attack conditions are met.

sense-vitals.notes: No damage spec and no scaling block: the 1d6-per-3-levels progression describes sneak attack dice added to a later attack roll, not damage this spell deals when cast.

effects.target: A 10-foot emanation around you opens the minds of everyone nearby. Every living creature in the area other than you gains a +5 bonus on Perception checks; sighted creatures gain low-light vision and creatures with a sense of smell gain scent. On top of that, the first time each round that a creature in the area takes damage, it takes an extra 2d6 points of damage of that same type - and you are exempt from that extra damage even though you stand in the area. Will negates.
effects.note: Every part of this lands on creatures other than the caster, and the spell has no targets - it is an emanation centred on a personal-range caster. A skill_mod or sense spec would grant the bonus to the one creature the prose excludes. The 2d6 is also conditional on being damaged, repeats once per round, and copies whatever damage type triggered it.

sensory-amplifier.notes: Refused to convert the +5 Perception, low-light vision and scent: the prose says 'all living creatures other than you', and the engine would apply them to you. The 2d6 fails three of the brief's tests at once - wrong creature, repeating, and no fixed damage type.

effects.target: The target's senses are overloaded. For the duration it must succeed at a Will save, at this spell's DC, before it can perform any standard or full-round action. Failing that save costs it the action that triggered it. Succeeding lets the action happen but does not end the spell, so the next action forces another save.
effects.note: A save repeated for every action taken over the whole duration, with action loss as the penalty. The vocabulary has no repeated-save gate and no 'loses its action' outcome.

sensory-overload.notes: The corpus save 'Will negates (see text)' is the initial save; the per-action saves described here are separate and cannot be represented.

effects.target: Restores the senses of a severed humanoid or monstrous humanoid head killed within the past day, fixed to a pole, spear, branch or other stable object - moving the head or its mount ends the spell. The head has darkvision 60 feet and low-light vision, swivels to look anywhere, and has +5 on Perception. Within 30 feet of it you may shift your senses into it as a standard action, seeing and hearing from its position with its darkvision and low-light vision and using its Perception instead of your own; while you do, your own body is blind and deaf until you spend a free action to return. At creation you imprint one triggering condition, as magic mouth, which can never afterwards be changed - any humanoid coming into view, a particular rival approaching, a guard animal being killed, anything the head could see. Within 30 feet you know the instant it triggers, and which skull triggered if you have several; this wakes you from normal sleep but does not otherwise break your concentration. The head cannot speak, think or act beyond turning itself, though other spells such as magic mouth can still be cast on it.
effects.note: The senses and the +5 Perception belong to the severed head, which is an object this spell animates, not to the caster.

sentry-skull.notes: No sense or skill_mod specs: darkvision, low-light vision and +5 Perception are the skull's, and the caster only borrows them by shifting senses into it.

effects.target: Hides a symbol in a written work of at least 25 words. When someone deliberately reads the text - merely seeing it is not enough - and has line of sight from the symbol, a large sepia serpent springs out and strikes. The reader gets a Reflex save; on a success the snake bursts in brown light, dun smoke and a loud noise. On a failure the reader is engulfed in a shimmering amber field of force and immobilised until you release it or 1d4 days plus 1 day per caster level have passed. Inside the field the subject does not age, breathe, hunger, sleep or regain spells and is unaware of everything around it, held in suspended animation. The field gives no protection from physical injury, so it can still be hurt or even killed - though a dying subject neither loses hit points nor stabilises until the spell ends. The sigil cannot be spotted by normal observation and detect magic shows only that the whole text is magical. Dispel magic removes it; erase destroys the entire page. It can be combined with spells that hide or garble text, such as secret page.
effects.note: A trap that fires when a reader triggers it, not when the spell is cast, and on a creature chosen by circumstance rather than by the caster. The amber field is suspended animation rather than any condition in the vocabulary.

sepia-snake-sigil.notes: The corpus duration bundles two different clocks - the sigil is permanent until discharged, and the imprisonment then lasts 1d4 days + 1 day/level. Recorded the sigil's own duration as until_discharged and left the imprisonment clock in the prose, since the schema cannot hold two sequential durations.

effects.target: invisibility
effects.note: The target is rendered invisible as part of this spell.

effects.target: unconscious
effects.note: The prose says an affected creature 'becomes comatose and is effectively in a state of suspended animation until the spell ends'. Recorded as unconscious, the vocabulary's nearest exact state - flagged as a translation for a reviewer, not a guess at an unstated condition. Applies only to creatures; an object target gets nothing here.

effects.target: Divination spells cannot detect or locate the target at all, and there is no save against that or against the invisibility - the Will save only stops an attended or magical object being sequestered in the first place. The subject can still be found by touch or by devices.
effects.note: The divination blocking has no effect type.

sequester.notes: Only condition mapping in this partition: 'comatose' to unconscious. Called out explicitly so it can be reversed at review if the engine treats unconscious as dying rather than as suspended animation.

effects.target: Erases a willing creature's memory of either one event lasting no more than 1 minute per caster level, or everything it knows about a single topic as the GM defines one - a particular battle, or an entire plot against a king. The memories are stored in the gem used to cast it. Shattering the gem returns them, so long as gem and creature are within 30 feet of each other. The spell stays on the gem, not on the creature: it can be dispelled, which shatters the gem, but the creature radiates no magic, and neither dispelling nor antimagic on the creature brings the memories back. If the gem is shattered or dispelled out of range, the thoughts are lost forever short of wish or miracle. Detect thoughts, zone of truth, discern lies and the like cannot reach the removed memories, though careful questioning may expose the gaps or reveal that the spell was used. The creature does not remember what was taken until the gem is broken.
effects.note: Memory removal stored in an object; nothing in the vocabulary reaches it.

sequester-thoughts.notes: Corpus duration is 'permanent until discharged (see text)'.

effects.target: Fills one creature per caster level with tranquility. Any of them that tries to commit violence is struck with wracking pain, taking 3d6 points of nonlethal damage each round it attempts to harm another creature. They may still defend themselves if attacked, and may use Combat Expertise, fight defensively or take the total defense action without triggering the damage at all.
effects.note: The 3d6 is conditional on the target choosing violence and repeats every round it keeps doing so. A damage spec would deal it once, at casting, to targets who may never raise a hand.

serenity.notes: Refused to convert the 3d6: conditional and per-round, both of which the brief names as narrative cases.

effects.target: The joints of an armoured foe's armour seize as otherworldly chains wrap it. A target in heavy metal armour that fails its Reflex save is staggered; one that succeeds is entangled instead. A target in light or medium metal armour that fails is entangled; one that succeeds is unaffected. A target wearing no armour, or nonmetallic armour, is unaffected either way.
effects.note: Which condition lands depends on the weight of the target's armour as well as on the save, so the outcome is a two-by-two table. A save_gate has one on_failure and one on_success branch and would apply the heavy-armour results to a target in light armour.

serren-s-armor-lock.notes: Both conditions are in the vocabulary but neither can be emitted safely - the branch is on the target's equipment, which no spec can test.

effects.target: one willing creature per caster level is instantly clad in a suit of armour you choose for it, and counts as having donned that armour properly
effects.note: Each subject must be able to wear and properly fit the armour chosen for it and cannot already be wearing armour. The armour must be empty - it cannot be pulled off another wearer.

serren-s-swift-girding.notes: Grants no bonus of its own; the AC comes from the armour, which the sheet already knows how to apply.

effects.target: Forces the spirits inside the target dormant. Against a medium with a spirit in its body, a spiritualist with a phantom in its consciousness, or anyone else using spirit or phantom class features, a failed save leaves that spirit or phantom powerless and suppresses every benefit it gives its host, bonus feats and spells known included. Where the spirit is instead a creature using a possession effect - possess object, possession, a ghost's malevolence - the spell targets the possessing creature rather than its host, and a failed save leaves it dazed for the duration without exorcising it.
effects.note: Two different outcomes on two different creatures, and which one applies decides who the spell even targets. Emitting dazed would daze a medium who should merely lose its spirit's benefits.

sessile-spirit.notes: Dazed is in the vocabulary but only fits one of the two branches, and the branch also changes the target.

effects.target: will
effects.note: One living target, Will negates.

effects.target: The cursed target also cannot spend hero points for the duration. Dispel magic, remove curse and similar effects lift the curse.
effects.note: Hero points are a table-level resource the effect vocabulary does not model.

severed-fate.notes: Clean case: single target, single stated condition, single stated save.

effects.target: Summons a set of Small or Medium masterwork restraints - manacles, or fetters made for the ankles - along with their key, to your person. The Disable Device DC to open them locked is 15 + your caster level + your primary casting ability modifier. They normally appear in your hands, but as part of casting you may make a melee touch attack: if it hits and the creature then fails a Reflex save, fetters clasp onto it, or manacles lock you and it together, or manacles bind its limbs in front of or behind it as you prefer. Cast as a full-round action you may make touch attacks against two creatures in reach and, if both hit and both fail their saves, manacle the two together. At 6th level or higher you may make them mithral or summon Tiny or Large restraints; at 12th, Diminutive or Huge. With an emerald worth at least 1,000 gp as a material component you may, once during the duration as a standard action, affect any creature bound by them as dimensional anchor for 1 minute per caster level. At 18th level with such an emerald the restraints gain hardness 30 and 60 hit points and cannot be broken by a Strength check at all - the emerald must be worth 2,000 gp if you also want the dimensional anchor. Recasting before the duration lapses either makes a new set or resets the old one's duration, which needs no touch so long as you are on the same plane, though an expensive component must be supplied again to keep a special effect. When it ends the restraints vanish along with anything they were doing.
effects.note: Conjured gear with its own statistics, delivered by a touch attack and a save. The vocabulary has no restraint condition matching manacles, and grappled or pinned would both be wrong.

effects.target: shadow conjuration
effects.note: Mimics conjuration spells of 8th level or lower rather than the lower cap of the base spell.

effects.target: The illusory conjurations deal four fifths - 80% - of their normal damage to nonbelievers, and their nondamaging effects are 80% likely to work against nonbelievers.
effects.note: The damage is the mimicked spell's, reduced by a percentage. There is no fixed dice expression here at all until a caster picks which spell to imitate.

shades.notes: Duration omitted: the corpus records 'see text' and the real duration is whichever spell is being mimicked. Emitting a value would invent one.

effects.target: The target's own shadow becomes a tether to the square it stands in. It can move up to 5 feet from that square freely. Going further requires a bull rush combat maneuver check against a CMB of 10 + half your caster level + your Intelligence modifier if you are a witch or wizard, or your Charisma modifier if a bard or sorcerer, with a -1 penalty for every 5 feet between it and the tethered square. Failing wastes the move and it gets no further away; failing by 10 or more drags it 5 feet back toward the square and knocks it prone; beating the check by 10 or more ends the spell. It does nothing to creatures that cast no shadow or reflection, and it ends if the target teleports or leaves the plane.
effects.note: The prone only happens on failing an opposed check by 10 or more, on a move the target may never attempt. Emitting apply_condition prone would knock it down at casting.

effects.target: you wield a shadowy spiked chain as though fully proficient with spiked chains, and any feats or abilities you have for spiked chains apply to it; it functions as a +2 vicious spiked chain
effects.note: The chain exists only while you carry it - dropping it, handing it over or being disarmed makes it vanish and ends the spell.

effects.target: The chain sheds darkness in a 10-foot-radius spread around you, lowering the light level by one step but never below dim light. Its enhancement bonus rises to +3 at caster level 11th, +4 at 15th and +5 at 19th. When the spell ends you may make a Will save against it: succeed and all the damage the vicious quality did to you vanishes, but if you are dead or unconscious when it ends you automatically fail and that damage stays.
effects.note: The vicious quality's damage to the wielder is the weapon's, dealt on your own attacks, and the enhancement bonus climbs with caster level, which the corpus scaling schema cannot express.

shadow-barbs.notes: No damage spec: a vicious weapon hurts its wielder each time it hits, which is per-attack and belongs to the granted weapon, not to the spell.

effects.target: You trade your material body for the essence of the Plane of Shadow and become a living shadow. In bright or normal light you are visible as an unattached shadow; in dim light or darkness you have total concealment, though only ordinary concealment against creatures with darkvision. You are incorporeal for most purposes but cannot fly or pass through solid objects or creatures. You move at your normal speed along any surface including vertical ones and liquids, and difficult terrain never slows you. Your size is unchanged. You can speak, cast spells and act mentally, but you have no physical substance, cannot manipulate objects and cannot attack physically, though you may deliver touch spells as incorporeal touch attacks. Your equipment merges into the shadow body, so you cannot cast spells with material components unless they are prepared with Eschew Materials.
effects.note: Becoming incorporeal changes how a dozen subsystems resolve at once; the vocabulary has no polymorph or incorporeality type.

effects.target: Drinking this extract changes every bomb you create and throw for the duration. It does not interfere with discoveries that modify your bombs, but only one 'bomb admixture' formula can be active at a time - drinking another ends this one. When a bomb of yours hits a direct target, shadowy substance covers that target and up to three creatures taking splash damage, your choice. Each affected creature must succeed at a Fortitude save or gain concealment while also treating every other creature as having concealment, for the rest of this admixture's duration. This does not ignore spell resistance.
effects.note: The effect fires on each bomb thrown during the duration, against whoever that bomb hits - not on any creature at the moment this extract is drunk. Concealment is also not in the condition vocabulary.

shadow-bomb-admixture.notes: Real finding: concealment and total concealment have no representation - they are neither a condition nor a typed modifier, and several spells in this partition grant them.

effects.target: a pair of semi-real claws forms over your hands, granting you two primary claw attacks dealing 1d4 points of damage if you are Medium, or 1d3 if you are Small
effects.note: Recorded as granted attacks. The dice belong to the claws when they hit, not to the spell when it is cast.

effects.target: Each claw that hits also deals 1 point of Strength damage, which a successful Fortitude save against this spell's DC negates.
effects.note: Conditional on landing a claw attack, and repeatable on every hit for the whole duration, so it cannot be an ability_damage spec fired at casting.

shadow-claws.notes: No damage or ability_damage spec: this is the brief's granted-natural-attack case.

effects.target: Shapes quasi-real illusions from the Plane of Shadow, mimicking any sorcerer or wizard conjuration (summoning) or conjuration (creation) spell of 3rd level or lower. Shadow conjurations are one fifth as strong as the real thing, but work at full strength on anyone who believes them. Any creature interacting with it may make a Will save to see through it; a disbelieving creature takes only 20% damage, and a non-damage special effect is only 20% likely to occur. Whatever the disbelief save does, the creature still gets any save the mimicked spell allows, but at a DC set by this spell's level (4th) rather than the mimicked spell's. Everything created allows spell resistance even if the mimicked spell would not. Shadow objects and substances work normally except against disbelievers, on whom they are 20% likely to work. A shadow creature has one fifth the hit points of the real thing, deals normal damage and has all normal abilities and weaknesses - but against a creature that recognises it, its damage is 20% of normal, its non-lethal special abilities are only 20% likely to work (rolled separately for each use and each character), and its AC bonuses are one fifth as large. A creature that saves sees transparent images over vague shadowy forms. Objects always succeed at their Will saves.
effects.note: The spell has no effects of its own - it borrows another spell chosen at casting and scales it by a percentage. There is no damage, condition or duration to convert until that choice is made.

shadow-conjuration.notes: Duration omitted: the corpus records 'see text' and the real duration is whichever spell is being mimicked.

effects.target: shadow conjuration
effects.note: Duplicates conjuration (summoning) and conjuration (creation) spells of 6th level or lower rather than 3rd.

effects.target: The illusory conjurations deal three fifths - 60% - of normal damage to nonbelievers, and nondamaging effects are 60% likely to work against them.
effects.note: The only differences from the base spell the prose states.

shadow-conjuration-greater.notes: Duration omitted for the same reason as the base spell.

effects.target: you wreathe yourself in a quasi-real dragon form, gaining two primary claw attacks dealing 1d6 plus your caster level in slashing damage and a primary bite dealing 1d8 plus your caster level in piercing damage, plus shadowy wings giving you a fly speed equal to your base speed with good manoeuvrability
effects.note: Granted natural attacks; their dice are the attacks', not the spell's. The fly speed copies your own base speed rather than naming a number, so it cannot be a speed spec.

effects.target: The shadowy natural weapons are only half as strong as real ones, though they work at full strength against anyone who believes them real. Each creature gets one Will save the first time you strike it; on a success it takes half damage from these attacks for the rest of the spell. If you beat a creature's spell resistance on your first attack against it, it stays vulnerable for the duration; if you do not, it is immune for the duration.
effects.note: The disbelief and spell resistance checks happen on first contact with each creature, not at casting.

effects.target: Casts a quasi-real illusory version of any psychic, sorcerer or wizard enchantment spell of 2nd level or lower, drawn from the Shadow Plane. It works normally unless the affected creature succeeds at a Will save. Against a disbeliever a damaging effect is one fifth as strong, or only 20% likely to occur, and a special effect other than damage is likewise one fifth as strong or 20% likely. Whatever the disbelief save does, the creature still gets any save or spell resistance the mimicked spell allows, at a DC set by this spell's level (3rd) rather than the mimicked spell's. Objects, mindless creatures and creatures immune to mind-affecting effects succeed at their Will saves automatically.
effects.note: Borrows another spell chosen at casting; nothing fixed to convert.

shadow-enchantment.notes: Duration omitted: corpus records 'see text' and the duration is the mimicked spell's.

effects.target: shadow enchantment
effects.note: Mimics psychic, sorcerer and wizard enchantment spells of 5th level or lower rather than 2nd.

effects.target: If it is recognised for what it is, it is three fifths - 60% - as effective, rather than one fifth.
effects.note: The only difference from the base spell the prose states.

shadow-enchantment-greater.notes: Duration omitted for the same reason as the base spell.

effects.target: Wisps of protective darkness wait on you. The moment you drop below 0 hit points or fall unconscious the spell discharges, shunting your body into a hidden alcove on the Shadow Plane. You stabilise immediately but cannot wake or act until the second duration runs out. As you vanish a quasi-real shadow duplicate of you appears where you fell, as though made by shadow conjuration, acting on your initiative under your control. It is one quarter as real as you, appears with 25% of your full hit points, and any creature that fails a Will save believes it is you. It has the same equipment-based bonuses you do but deals only a quarter of your normal damage, and it can cast any spell you can from your own reserve at a caster level one quarter of yours. Whatever your alignment, the duplicate is neutral evil, though it will not harm your friends or allies. When the second duration expires the duplicate vanishes and your body returns to where you disappeared; destroying the duplicate ends the spell at once and returns you the same way.
effects.note: A contingency that fires on you dropping, not at casting, and then creates a controlled duplicate. Nothing in the vocabulary expresses either half.

shadow-endurance.notes: Corpus duration is 'hours/level until discharged, then minutes/level'. Recorded the first clock - the hours/level wait for the trigger - and left the post-discharge minutes/level in the prose, since the schema cannot hold two sequential durations. Same limitation as sepia snake sigil.

effects.target: Draws energy from the Plane of Shadow to cast a quasi-real version of any sorcerer or wizard evocation spell of 4th level or lower. Damaging spells work normally unless the affected creature succeeds at a Will save; a disbelieving creature takes only one fifth damage, and a special effect other than damage is one fifth as strong or only 20% likely to occur. Recognised for what it is, a damaging spell deals 20% damage. Whatever the disbelief save does, the creature still gets any save or spell resistance the mimicked spell allows, at a DC set by this spell's level (5th) rather than the mimicked spell's. Nondamaging effects work normally except against disbelievers, on whom they have no effect at all. Objects succeed at their Will saves automatically.
effects.note: Borrows another spell chosen at casting; there is no damage, condition or duration of its own to convert.

shadow-evocation.notes: Duration omitted: corpus records 'see text' and the duration is the mimicked spell's.

effects.target: shadow evocation
effects.note: Mimics sorcerer and wizard evocation spells of 7th level or lower rather than 4th.

effects.target: Recognised for what it is, a damaging spell deals three fifths - 60% - damage rather than one fifth.
effects.note: The only difference from the base spell the prose states.

shadow-evocation-greater.notes: Duration omitted for the same reason as the base spell.

effects.target: A slashing motion with the focus cuts a rift to the Plane of Shadow, filling a stationary 30-foot emanation with shadowy energy and dropping the light level by one step as darkness does. Shadow subschool spells that have reduced effects when disbelieved, such as shadow evocation, have those reduced effects raised by 20 percentage points, to a maximum of 90%, against targets inside the area. The rift also draws attention from the far side: dismissing the spell as a standard action carries a 5% chance per full round it was active of summoning a single evangelist kyton under your command, as summon monster V, or an interlocutor kyton instead if your caster level is 16th or higher. A kyton called this way stays for as many rounds as the spell's duration would have had left had you not dismissed it. Successfully summoning one is a lawful and evil act, as though you had cast a spell with the lawful and evil descriptors.
effects.note: It modifies other shadow spells cast into the area and summons on dismissal by percentile roll; neither has an effect type.

effects.target: You step between shadows to a point within close range without needing line of sight, leaving a shadowy image of yourself behind and arriving wrapped in shadow, with a free Stealth check to hide where you land. Creatures that lose opposed Perception checks usually do not realise you have left, unless they know this spell and recognise it; any attack on your old position scatters the shadows and reveals your absence to anyone who can see it. For 1 round the shadow around you grants concealment, a 20% miss chance. It does not work at all unless there are shadows within 5 feet of where you start, you cannot travel through your own shadow, and choosing a destination with no shadows drops you at the nearest shadow within range - possibly the one you left from.
effects.note: Teleportation, plus concealment, which is neither a condition nor a typed modifier in the vocabulary.

shadow-jaunt.notes: Corpus duration is 'instantaneous and 1 round (see text)'. Recorded the instantaneous travel; the 1 round of concealment that follows is in the prose, the schema having no way to hold two durations at once.

effects.target: A shadowy aura of doubt settles on one creature per three caster levels. Every target perceives all illumination as one light level darker, to a minimum of darkness though never supernatural darkness, and this happens even on a successful save. Fleeting shadows of regret and anxiety distract them: at the start of each of their turns each must succeed at a Will save or be staggered for 1 round. A good-aligned target takes -4 on those saves; an evil-aligned target gets +4 instead.
effects.note: The staggered condition is decided by a fresh save at the start of every one of the target's turns, so it cannot be applied once at casting. The alignment modifiers to that save also have no representation.

shadow-of-doubt.notes: Staggered is in the vocabulary but is re-rolled every round; emitting apply_condition would stagger the target for the whole duration with no save.

effects.target: You pour your life force and psyche into your own shadow, giving it independent life as an undead shadow. Your physical body lies comatose while you project, and has no shadow or reflection for the duration. Projecting, you gain a shadow's darkvision, defensive abilities, fly speed, racial Stealth modifier and Strength damage attack, but not its create spawn ability and not its skill ranks or Hit Dice - your shadow has your own Hit Dice and hit points. The projection has the undead type and can be turned or otherwise affected as undead. If it is slain you snap back to your body at -1 hit points, dying, and must start making Constitution checks to stabilise.
effects.note: Becoming a different creature. The borrowed senses, speed and attack are all 'a shadow's', read off that monster's entry rather than stated as numbers here.

shadow-projection.notes: No sense or speed specs: darkvision and the fly speed come from the Bestiary shadow entry, and this prose names no ranges or values to emit.

effects.target: Standing in dim light or darkness, you enter a shadow or patch of darkness and are carried along a coiling path of shadowstuff to another dim or dark spot within medium range.
effects.note: Teleportation; the vocabulary has no travel type.
